2.7.1Relations between Sources and the Scope of Actual Use ​

In briefSources have genealogies, and reading has a scope. Transcription, republication, or revision of a file does not automatically add independent evidence by multiplying URLs.

Reading a table of contents, an abstract, relevant chapters, or the full text should be recorded separately. Finding a link, completing a download, and understanding an argument are also different actions. Relations between sources should be retained for different analyses of the same data, a preprint and its published version, and an original report and an institution's account of it. Citation counts must not be added up as independent reproductions. When a version changes outcomes, samples, or reporting definitions, first explain the changes, then compare conclusions.

A theory's historical adoption, mere mention, explicit restriction or rejection, compatibility with the current text, and a new connection now proposed by the analyst are distinct matters. Failure to find a record of adoption is not the same as its never having been considered; transcribing a catalog is not the same as checking the original document. Failure to obtain a document within one research window does not mean that other researchers or the project as a whole lack it.

The generation, preservation, destruction, opening, and retrieval of archives, as well as narrative choices, can each cause absence. Absence has the corresponding force as counterevidence only when it is clear that a certain kind of event should have left records that could be found. Inaccurate dates in oral accounts still need correction, while the way the account is told may also be important material for understanding memory and experience. Neither cancels the other.

2.7.1Note

Understanding this section

2.7.1 Relationships among sources and actual scope of use

Sources have genealogies, and reading has a scope. Transcription, republication, or revision of a file does not automatically add independent evidence by multiplying URLs.

Record separately whether only the contents list, the abstract, relevant chapters, or the full text were read. Finding a link establishes discovery of an entry point; downloading establishes acquisition of a file; understanding a passage's argument still requires actually examining its premises and material. Reading only relevant passages can honestly support bounded facts within them; do not enlarge that reading scope into a claim of full-text review.

Preserve relationships among different analyses of the same data, preprints and final versions, and original reports and institutional retellings. Another algorithm may expose errors in the original analysis without automatically generating new observations; a final version may also change the sample, outcomes, or definitions. List changes before comparing: similar titles alone justify neither merging them nor treating them as replications.

The history of a theory also requires distinguishing actual adoption, mere mention, explicit limitation or rejection, compatibility with the current text, and a new connection proposed by today's analyst. Each historical claim needs its own record. “Compatible as seen today” does not establish that the author was influenced by it then; failure to find evidence of adoption is insufficient to say “the author never considered it.”

Absence from an archive follows multiple filters: whether an event generated a record, whether it was preserved or destroyed, whether it was opened to access, whether retrieval can find it, and whether the narrator ultimately selected it. Absence has corresponding counterevidential force only when events of that kind should have left discoverable traces. Failure to obtain a file within one research window does not mean other researchers or the entire project lack it.

Date errors in oral accounts should still be corrected, while the manner of narration may supply material about memory, experience, and meaning. One chronological error does not make the whole oral account worthless; the account's value does not justify refusing to correct factual misplacement either. Evaluate different uses separately.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Premise: number of source files, number of underlying datasets, and scope of reading are three different objects of measurement.

  2. 2

    Connection: source relationships must be established before distinguishing new material, reanalysis, transcription, version changes, and repeated retellings; reading status determines what can currently be personally verified.

  3. 3

    Historical inference: upgrading “not found” to “never happened” requires additional support that traces should exist and could be retrieved; otherwise report only that material was not obtained within the current scope.

  4. 4

    Conclusion: cite within the scope actually read and evaluate sources by information actually added; do not replace independence with counts of files, citations, or URLs.

  5. 5

    Responsibility: remain accountable for correctable content such as dates and numbers, while preserving the distinctive contributions of different materials to different questions.

Distinctions to keep clear

The full text exists

An opportunity to obtain the complete text may exist.

≠

The full text was read in this inquiry

The whole text was actually accessed and examined; existence or downloading cannot substitute for this.

Multiple versions of a shared source

May contain valuable revisions and reanalyses.

≠

Independent replication

Requires an account of independent observations or design; the number of versions does not determine it.

Not found in the current search

The status of material within the current search window.

≠

Never existed historically

A stronger claim over all relevant times and places, carrying far greater evidential responsibility.

Factual date accuracy

Used for ordering events and checking facts.

≠

Meaningfulness of expressed memory

Used to understand narration and experience; both evaluations can proceed together.

Teaching construction: which conclusions are affected by an incorrect date in an oral account?Teaching scenario

AssumptionsThe interview and dates are teaching stipulations, referring to no real person or actual archive.

Suppose an interview dates an event to 2010, while a verifiable document dates it to 2012. Correct the event date and chronological inferences that depend on it. But if the question concerns how the interviewee connects the event to another life stage, the narrative itself can still serve as material on how memory is organized. This does not warrant inferring that the interviewee is lying, nor retaining the wrong year as a fact.

BoundaryIllustrates evaluation by use, without psychological diagnosis or endorsement of any real oral account.

2.7.2Evidence Independence and the Propagation of Defects ​

In briefA different analysis of the same material may indeed add knowledge, but does not add an independent sample. Finding a discrepancy should initially suspend only conclusions that actually depend on it.

Independence must be judged relative to the claim being supported. Adding later outcomes to the same random assignment can add temporal and outcome information. Testing the same data with another algorithm can uncover implementation or interpretation problems. Neither increases the number of independent randomizations or original cohorts. Conversely, studies on the same subject but with different underlying samples must not be merged merely because their names are similar. Records should specify shared data, common measurements, version inheritance, and genuinely new observations, rather than turn a file count into an evidence score.

Traceable dependencies should be retained between source values, transcriptions, model inputs, derived statistics, and judgments in the text. When a local discrepancy is found, first distinguish conflict concerning the same object, legitimate differences between different objects, and apparent inconsistency caused by display precision. Then suspend the precise conclusions that actually depend on that discrepancy. Reconciliation of the component sum with the total does not by itself validate every component, nor does a source anomaly reveal the cause of a discrepancy on its own. Other judgments with independent support should continue to be used within their actual scope.

2.7.2Note

Understanding this section

2.7.2 Evidence independence and propagation of defects

A different analysis of the same material may indeed add knowledge, but does not add an independent sample. Finding a discrepancy should initially suspend only conclusions that actually depend on it.

Independence is not an unconditional yes/no label. Long-term follow-up of the same randomized allocation adds information on time and outcomes, but not another randomization; rechecking the same material with another algorithm adds implementation and interpretation checks, but not a new original cohort. Conversely, two studies with the same topic name but different underlying samples must not be forcibly merged based solely on their titles.

Source relationships should preserve shared data, common measurements, version inheritance, and new observations. Specify which stage is independent: data may be shared while analytical implementations are independent; measurement methods may be shared while samples of objects are independent. Evaluating a particular claim requires identifying its dependence on these stages, not converting file counts into evidence scores.

On finding a numerical discrepancy, first determine whether it is a conflict about the same object, a legitimate difference between different objects, or an apparent difference in display precision. Cases versus person-occurrences, cumulative versus new counts, onset date versus death date, and the whole population versus a threshold-defined subgroup need not be equal. If a genuine conflict remains unexplained, suspend precise conclusions depending on that number and trace the chain “source value → transcription → model input → derived quantity → main text.”

Agreement of sums is a check, but cannot by itself certify every component. One component increasing while another decreases can leave the total unchanged; conversely, an anomaly does not immediately identify transcription error, fabrication, or actual change as its cause. First report the locatable discrepancy and affected scope; do not fill in causes on behalf of the evidence.

Other judgments with independent grounds can continue to be used within their scope. Only failure of a common source, key premise, or object boundary blocks all related outputs. Proposition-by-proposition handling allows correction without concealing a problem or inflating a local issue into an unsupported wholesale rejection.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Premise one: new information can come from new samples, times, measurements, or analyses; these additions are not the same kind of independence.

  2. 2

    Premise two: derived conclusions depend only on their actual inputs and premises, so error propagation has specific paths.

  3. 3

    Connection: first align numbers by object, definition, unit, window, and precision, then determine whether there is a genuine conflict or a legitimate difference; for a genuine conflict, suspend conclusions along the dependency path.

  4. 4

    Conclusion: register both independence and downgrading claim by claim; unaffected independent grounds are not invalidated together with a local anomaly.

  5. 5

    Actual calculation: the 43 dated rows for known onset dates in Snow's Table I sum to 571; adding 45 with unknown onset dates gives the table's total of 616. This agreement checks only aggregation, not the correctness of the allocation across dates.

Distinctions to keep clear

Independent data

New underlying observations or cohorts.

≠

Independent reanalysis

A different implementation on the same underlying sample; it may reveal errors but does not count another group of people.

Genuine conflict

The claims still cannot coexist after aligning object, unit, and time.

≠

Legitimate difference

The objects, denominators, or indicators being compared were different to begin with.

Agreement of the total

The sum of components matches the total.

≠

Correct components

Each component has correct provenance, classification, and definitions; further checking is required.

Local anomaly

Affects particular values and derived conclusions.

≠

Failure of a shared premise

May block every output depending on it, with a broader scope.

Mathematical teaching construction: the same total with both components wrongTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThese numbers are purely a teaching construction, not Snow's data or any actual dataset.

Suppose the true components are 40 and 60, totaling 100. If transcribed as 45 and 55, the total is still 100. Passing the total check does not guarantee correct components. Text using only an independently checked total may be unaffected by this allocation error; text using the two groups' proportions or difference requires suspending the relevant inference.

BoundaryDemonstrates error propagation without accusing any real author of fabrication or identifying a particular transcription error.

Snow's Table I: check both the sum and the strength of the wordingDocumented case

Table I in the current transcription lists 45 cases with unknown onset dates; the other 43 dated rows sum to 571, for a total of 616. A further local check shows 20 on September 6 and 28 on September 7, so “decreased every day” cannot be used as a strictly monotonic numerical proposition. This section does not speculate about the cause of the discrepancy, but only limits the corresponding wording.

What does not follow

  • Snow's Table I gives 20 onsets of ultimately fatal cases on September 6 and 28 on September 7. Thus, the text's “decreased every day” cannot mechanically be read as a strictly monotonic sequence. This local counterexample does not erase the overall decline, nor determine the cause of a difference involving transcription or the original wording.
  • This lesson checks only the aggregate and these two daily values in the current digital transcription; it does not claim word-for-word collation of the original death registers. The 43 dated rows are not 43 independent studies.
  • 571+45=616 does not establish that the 45 unknown dates can be allocated arbitrarily, or that the complete number of infections is known.

Scope and open questions

Aggregates and local changes within the same source can be checked exactly, directly demonstrating discrepancy classification and the narrowing of conclusions without fabricating causes for anomalies.

No. Additional information about time and outcomes is worth retaining, but neither allocation nor the original cohort has thereby been replicated.

If a table's total equals the sum of its components, does that establish that every component is correct?

No. Component errors can cancel each other; source values, units, classifications, and transcription still require checking.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If a figure for one day is disputed, why should every judgment in the same book not immediately be withdrawn?

First determine which conclusions actually depend on the number; other judgments with independent material may remain. Expand the suspension only if a common source or boundary has failed.

2.8Core Terminology Locks ​

In brief‘Cost’, ‘repair’, ‘choice’, and ‘responsibility’ are everyday words, but each carries different conditions for judgment. Fixing their meanings prevents a sentence from silently changing meaning during an inference.
Codes used in this section (4)
  • C7Local Improvement and Cross-Boundary Spillover
  • D3Scale Transformation
  • E5Testing Cross-Scale Transfer
  • G4Representational Closure and Object or Intervention Conversion

Once the following terms enter a judgment, they must satisfy their specified contracts. Their broad everyday meanings must not be substituted for those contracts.

Cost. First declare the quantity's type, unit, time window, accounting boundary, and cost-bearing position. Shifting may be traced only for quantities of the same type, or quantities of different types with an explicit conversion and accounting mapping. “Resources are occupied” is not the same as the existence of a unified cost across domains, nor does it establish any conservation principle.

Externality. First establish a cross-boundary causal channel and the positions across which its effects are distributed, then an institutional or accounting rule defining what is excluded from decision accounting. Without the latter, the effect can only be called a cross-boundary spillover, impact, or accounting gap. “Externality” must not be used to assign responsibility in advance.

The exclusion rule here may come from an explicit economic model or actual institutional and accounting arrangements. It does not require an advance determination of legal liability. The current inability to identify who bears legal liability does not prevent recording cross-boundary harm for which evidence already exists. C7 addresses cross-boundary spillovers and the positions across which they are distributed under its specified conditions. Where changes of scale are actually involved, D3/E5 must be checked separately; claims of closure failure or conversion of objects or interventions also require testing the corresponding G4. It does not cover all economic externalities or propagation in general.

Repair. The target identity criterion K* or functional criterion F* must be disclosed before results. Repair is not the same as recovery of a historical state, nor is it the same as improvement in value. Whether the target is justified, who decides it, and who may carry it out require separate review under N and O.

Selection and choice. First distinguish modes of systemic selection, choices by acting subjects, and governance choices. The systemic process of variation–differential retention–reproduction does not possess intent as a matter of course. A subject's decision is not the same as environmental selection. Governance choice additionally requires normative premises and authorization.

Responsibility and authorization. Uptake carriers, bearers of costs of the same type, beneficiaries, rights to stop, and responsible parties are registered separately. Actual execution, the greatest capability, being most affected, being most visible, or possessing knowledge cannot by themselves establish responsibility. Nor can an expansion of observational scope or confidence in explanation expand authority to act.

Bearing obligations requires a separate account of the relations among commitments, roles, causal contributions, benefits, capabilities, and applicable norms. These reasons may act together; no one of them can automatically settle the whole matter. Disclosing bounded obligations and their boundaries does not make anyone a person required to take up obligations without limit, unilaterally, and without the possibility of exit.

2.8Note

Understanding this section

2.8 Core terminology lock

‘Cost’, ‘repair’, ‘choice’, and ‘responsibility’ are everyday words, but each carries different conditions for judgment. Fixing their meanings prevents a sentence from silently changing meaning during an inference.

Cost is first a quantity of some type: its type, unit, time window, accounting boundary, and cost-bearing position must be stated. Cash, working hours, risk, and attention cannot simply be added; conversion requires an explicit valuation, measurement, or accounting mapping. Lower spending in one place does not mean a cost of the same type necessarily shifts elsewhere, much less establish a universal conservation of cost across domains. Occupation of resources is an observation; comparability with other quantities is a separate task.

Externality here involves two steps: first establish a cross-boundary causal channel and the positions across which effects are distributed, then specify which impact an economic model or actual institutional or accounting rule excludes from decision accounting. With only the first step, call it a cross-boundary spillover or impact; terminology must not assign responsibility in advance. The second step does not require prior determination of legal liability; inability to determine who is legally liable does not prevent recording supported cross-boundary harm.

Cross-boundary analysis also requires the right contract. C7 addresses spillovers and distributional positions under its specified conditions, not every economic externality or instance of transmission. Check D3/E5 separately only where scale actually changes; test the corresponding G4 only when claiming formal support for closure failure or object or intervention conversion. The word ‘external’ alone must not trigger every scale procedure.

Repair requires disclosure, before outcomes, of the target identity K* or function F*: which object identity or function is to be recovered. Repair may allow a new implementation rather than reproduce the historical form; recovery of a specified function also does not equal an improvement in value. Whether the target is justified, who decides it, and who may implement it remain subject to N and O review. The target must not be changed after seeing results to declare any change a successful repair.

Choice has three meanings. System selection is a process of variation, differential retention, and reproduction; it need not involve intention. Choice by an acting subject involves a subject deciding under conditions and must not be equated with environmental selection. Governance choice additionally requires comparisons of options, normative premises, and authorization; observing that an outcome was retained does not mean someone justifiably chose it.

Responsibility and authorization separately register the uptake carrier, bearer of costs of the same type, beneficiaries, right to stop, and responsible party. Being the actual implementer, the most capable, the most affected, the most visible, or the best informed does not by itself make someone infinitely responsible. Expanded observation or confidence in explanation does not expand jurisdiction J either.

Reasons for obligations may include commitments, roles, causal contributions, benefits, capabilities, and applicable norms; disclose how they jointly support specific obligations and their boundaries. Bounded obligations do not turn anyone into a unilateral, unlimited uptake party with no exit; arrangements for stopping, handoff, duration, and remedy are themselves part of responsibility judgments.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Premise: an everyday word often simultaneously carries descriptive, evaluative, and action-related meanings; mixing them allows a later step to borrow grounds the earlier step never supplied.

  2. 2

    First connection: costs first require the same type and unit or a valid conversion; externalities first require causation and exclusion rules; repair first requires K*/F*; choice first requires specifying the system, subject, or governance meaning.

  3. 3

    Second connection: where responsibility is involved, separately check roles, causation, commitments, benefits, capabilities, and norms instead of deriving total responsibility directly from one visible identity.

  4. 4

    Conclusion: locking meanings makes each step's missing conditions visible; ‘successful repair’ must not bypass value review, and ‘I understand’ must not bypass authorization.

  5. 5

    Evidential and normative responsibility: cross-boundary effects and cost-bearing positions require materials; exclusion rules require a basis in models or institutions; obligations and action ceilings require norms and valid authorization.

Distinctions to keep clear

Reduced spending

A change in an amount of money within a specified boundary, unit, and window.

≠

Lower unified cost

A stronger judgment across different cost bearers and quantity types, requiring grounds for conversion and allocation.

Cross-boundary impact

Has causation and distributional positions.

≠

Externality

Additionally specifies the rule excluding the impact from decision accounting; this is not prior determination of legal liability.

Repair

Meets K* or F* specified before outcomes.

≠

Improvement in value

A justified target and acceptable consequences, requiring additional normative assessment.

System selection

A process of differential retention.

≠

Subject/governance choice

The former requires a subject's decision; the latter additionally requires norms and permissions.

Uptake party or beneficiary

Records who actually bears or receives what.

≠

Responsible party

Bounded obligations supported by multiple reasons and norms; not automatically the same party.

Teaching construction: budget savings and time burdens cannot simply be conservedTeaching scenario

Assumptions100 yuan and 3 hours are teaching assumptions; an illustrative conversion is possible only after explicitly specifying conditions such as a single user and the same window.

Suppose an option reduces an institution's monthly spending by 100 yuan but makes a user wait an additional 3 hours. First record yuan/month and hours/person-visit separately, along with their bearers; do not write ‘total cost fell by 97’ or ‘100 yuan fully converted into 3 hours’. Only with an explicit valuation of v yuan per hour may 100−3v be written for a specified number of people and window. This v includes choices of value and measurement and must not be disguised as a universal constant of the world.

BoundaryDoes not estimate the net welfare of an actual option or allocate legal liability from these numbers.

Teaching construction: functional repair does not mean everything returns to its old formTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe equipment, load, error bound, and outcome are all conditional teaching assumptions, not a measurement report.

Suppose the pre-specified F* is ‘reading error no greater than e under a given load’. If valid measurement after component replacement shows F* is met, this may count as functional recovery within that contract; there is no need to claim that every original component has been restored. If the new component introduces additional safety risks or infringes others' rights, meeting the function criterion does not by itself justify the option.

BoundaryQualification as repair is limited to the specified function; justification, actual evidence, and implementation permissions are checked separately.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleTeaching boundary: the person who understands the system best is required to bear all maintenance costs permanently solely because ‘only you are capable’.

What it limitsCapability may be one reason for responsibility, but does not by itself imply an unlimited obligation with no exit.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleTeaching boundary: an organizational form survives competition, which is described as ‘the system intentionally selected the most justified institution’.

What it limitsDifferential retention has been replaced by a subject's intention and normative superiority; both additional claims lack grounds.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • This section specifies specialized meanings and conditions of use; definitions do not establish a universal conservation of cost or a shared purpose in the world.
  • Failure to determine legal liability does not prevent recording harm; recording harm also does not establish burden shares or authority to act.
  • Observational capability and authorization are different scale axes. Even complete knowledge of the situation still requires checking permissions for the particular object, action, territory, validity period, and withdrawal conditions.
  • Repair targets must not be arbitrarily rewritten after results; necessary changes require a new version that preserves outcomes under the original target.

Scope and open questions

This section fixes meanings and use contracts; teaching counterexamples directly expose substitutions of units, targets, intentions, and responsibilities. Historical facts are not forced into the definitions.

  2. 2

    Why does a function meeting its pre-specified target still not justify declaring ‘this is a good option and may be implemented immediately’?

  3. 3

    If A benefits most and B performs most of the implementation, may that alone identify one sole responsible party?

If pollution is recorded as harming others across a boundary, must legal liability first be determined before its impacts can be reported?

No. Recording causal harm, identifying accounting-exclusion rules, and determining legal liability are different tasks; supported impacts can be retained first.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Why does a function meeting its pre-specified target still not justify declaring ‘this is a good option and may be implemented immediately’?

Functional repair does not settle values, risks, permissions, action ceilings, or stopping conditions; N and O require separate checking.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If A benefits most and B performs most of the implementation, may that alone identify one sole responsible party?

No. Disclose the relations among commitments, roles, causal contributions, benefits, capabilities, and applicable norms, and bound the obligations.

2.9Missing Fields and Visibility States, Downgrading, Suspension, and Exit ​

In briefA blank should not simply be filled with ‘not available’. First distinguish whether something is not yet known, conceptually inapplicable, currently unobservable, or available but protected; then determine exactly which conclusion and action must be restricted.

Every contract field must fall within an explicit state, rather than be filled with vague wording.

Unknown: knowable in principle, but current evidence is insufficient.

Not applicable: the field has no valid counterpart in the current object contract; a reason must be stated.

Unobservable: materials cannot currently be obtained because of limits in measurement capability, the window, or the channel; this must not be rewritten as nonexistence.

Withheld for protection: materials exist, but disclosure would violate privacy, security, or other explicit protections. The basis for protection, minimum scope of non-disclosure, duration, and a trusted review path must be recorded.

When key variables are unknown, conditions under which the object is not applicable remain unaddressed, core channels are unobservable, or non-disclosure for protection cannot undergo trusted review, conclusions are downgraded successively to candidate hypotheses, lists of questions, or description only. When authorization to act is unclear, potential harm is irreversible, appeals and stopping are inaccessible, or the limits of professional capability would be exceeded, real-world action should be suspended and referred to an appropriate procedure. Downgrading is not analytical failure. It keeps the evidential ceiling, boundaries of power, and what is still unknown visible. Each downgrade is registered proposition by proposition with its dependencies and the effects of what is missing. Other judgments with independent support are not downgraded along with it; failure of a global source, common premise, or object boundary blocks all related outputs.

2.9Note

Understanding this section

2.9 Missing Fields and Visibility Statuses, Downgrading, Suspension, and Exit

A blank should not simply be filled with ‘not available’. First distinguish whether something is not yet known, conceptually inapplicable, currently unobservable, or available but protected; then determine exactly which conclusion and action must be restricted.

Unknown: knowable in principle, but current evidence is insufficient. State which materials are missing and what could change that status. Not applicable: the field has no valid counterpart in the current object contract, with reasons given; it does not mean ‘hard to fill, so omit it’. For example, where a purely natural process has no acting subject or authorization concept, the J axis may be inapplicable, but a researcher's intervention in that process may still require authorization. Objects and actions must not be conflated.

Unobservable: materials cannot currently be obtained because of measurement capabilities, time windows, or channels. This means neither nonexistence nor permanent unknowability; changing the window or measurement may change visibility, but missing facts must not be falsely presented as already obtained. Withheld for protection: materials do exist, but disclosure would violate privacy, safety, or explicit protections; record the grounds for protection, minimal scope, duration, and a credible review route.

The four statuses jointly describe knowledge and visibility; they must not silently become truth labels. An unknown must not be filled with 0, an inapplicable value must not be added to zero, unobservable must not be recorded as absent, and withheld for protection must not be described as the researcher lacking materials. State the appropriate status under the contract and, where needed, additionally record whether credible review is available.

Where key variables are missing, applicability is untreated, core channels are unobservable, or protected materials cannot undergo credible review, downgrade the affected claims to candidates, a list of questions, or description. This does not mechanically reduce every conclusion to one level; assess separately whether each missing condition is necessary. A factual count may be supported while a mechanistic explanation remains unresolved; both can coexist.

Action boundaries are assessed separately: unclear authorization, risks of irreversible harm, unavailable appeal or stopping mechanisms, or limits of professional capability should suspend real-world dispositions and lead into appropriate procedures. Safe clarification of materials and discussion of options may continue; this does not permit implementation under the label of ‘probing’. Exiting or withdrawing a claim also does not require erasing genuine records of failure.

Failure of a local premise affects only outputs that depend on it; failure of a global source, common premise, or object boundary blocks all related outputs. The difference concerns actual dependency scope, not willingness to acknowledge a problem. Preserving unknowns and downgrading makes evidential ceilings and boundaries of power visible, itself a responsible conclusion.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Premise: apparently identical blanks may have different causes; filling all with zero or no changes either the object facts or the field meanings.

  2. 2

    Classification: give each field an explicit status and reason; distinguish materials already available, materials missing, and materials that should not be disclosed.

  3. 3

    Dependency check: list the necessary inputs for each claim; restrict a claim when a necessary input is missing while retaining other independently grounded claims.

  4. 4

    Action check: incomplete evidence and incomplete authorization can each block disposition; severe irreversible risks, capability limits, and unavailable stopping mechanisms cannot be overridden by model confidence.

  5. 5

    Conclusion: downgrade, suspend, or exit according to the scope of the gap, preserving materials and previous records needed for reassessment; do not treat inability to observe as nonexistence.

Distinctions to keep clear

Unknown

An answer may be obtainable, but current grounds are insufficient.

≠

Not applicable

The field has no valid meaning for this object; reasons are required.

Unobservable

The current window or channel does not permit obtaining an observation.

≠

Nonexistent

A negative fact about the world, which does not automatically follow from the preceding status.

Protective nondisclosure

Materials exist; disclosure is restricted and credible review arranged.

≠

No one can review it

Further restricts the conclusion; protection does not exempt strong assertions from review.

Downgrading a conclusion

Reduces the strength that the evidence can support.

≠

Suspending real-world disposition

Stops action because of permissions, harm, appeals, or capability; these reasons may be independent.

Teaching construction: four blanks, four different answersTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThese are four teaching scenarios, containing no real personal data, experiments, or field measurements.

Suppose an analysis table contains: a daily total not yet obtained, marked unknown; a subject-authorization field for a purely natural process, marked not applicable after explaining the absence of an acting subject; an instantaneous peak beyond the instrument's range, marked unobservable; and an existing individual record involving privacy, marked withheld for protection after specifying protection grounds, scope, duration, and reviewers. The four cells must not all be filled with 0.

BoundarySpecific lawfulness and protective procedures require checking in the actual setting; the example authorizes neither collection, disclosure, nor disposition.

Teaching construction: one missing link does not zero out the entire pageTeaching scenario

Assumptions20 and the interface scenario are teaching assumptions; independence is an explicit premise, not an established fact.

Suppose independent counting records support ‘there are 20 requests in the queue’, while the explanation ‘congestion is caused by failure of interface A’ depends on interface logs not yet obtained. Retain the limited description of 20 requests and keep the mechanism as a candidate; if the count is later found to duplicate the same request, both the count and derived rates must be rechecked.

BoundaryDoes not claim that an actual system has 20 requests or a failed interface; it illustrates downgrading claim by claim only.

Local exclusion when ancient-DNA sample identity is unresolvedDocumented case

Skov et al.'s 2022 paper states that they could not be confident Chagyrskaya E was an individual distinct from D, so E was removed from subsequent analyses. This lesson uses it as an example of restricting use according to a specific identity gap, without retrospectively assigning the authors Xikari status codes.

SourceSkov et al. 2022, explanation of the treatment of sample EGenetic relationships: the paragraph on contamination of Chagyrskaya E, correction, and ‘cannot be confident…distinct individual’Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsSupports only the handling of this sample and its stated reasons; the genetic data were not recalculated for this lesson, and it does not establish that every other conclusion is error-free.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Empirical counterevidenceSkov et al. could not confirm that Chagyrskaya E was an individual distinct from D, so they removed sample E from subsequent analyses.

What it limitsUnclear identity affects eligibility to use that sample, rather than automatically invalidating every other supported kinship analysis.

Skov et al., Genetic insights into the social organization of Neanderthals

Teaching counterexampleTeaching boundary: a researcher records ‘not permitted to see the materials’ as ‘the materials do not exist’ and uses this to exclude an explanation.

What it limitsA visibility restriction has been presented as a negative fact; the corresponding exclusion judgment should be withdrawn to unresolved status.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • The four field statuses are not four truth values of the world; unknown, not_applicable, and invisibility must not all be encoded as numerical 0 and averaged.
  • Non-disclosure for protection must not justify coercing disclosure, nor become a permanent pass for strong claims that cannot be reviewed.
  • Local failure does not invariably contaminate the whole; but if object identity or a common source is broadly unreliable, suspension must extend to all related judgments.

Scope and open questions

An actual study discloses identity uncertainty and a local exclusion, showing how a gap corresponds to a scope of use; this is the same case as the preceding question, with an additional angle on evidence handling.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    If material exists but is withheld for privacy, should it be marked ‘unknown’ for convenience?

  2. 2

    If a mechanism's key input is missing but independent descriptive data are credible, must every conclusion be withdrawn?

  3. 3

    If the model is highly confident but authorization is unclear, may the action be tried once first?

If material exists but is withheld for privacy, should it be marked ‘unknown’ for convenience?

Do not substitute one status for another. Record non-disclosure for protection, its grounds, minimal scope, duration, and credible review route; separately state how much the public or current analyst can support.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If a mechanism's key input is missing but independent descriptive data are credible, must every conclusion be withdrawn?

Not necessarily. Downgrade the mechanism judgment that depends on the missing input while retaining the independent description; expand the scope if a common source or object boundary fails.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If the model is highly confident but authorization is unclear, may the action be tried once first?

Confidence cannot confer authority. The relevant action should be suspended while authority and procedures for stopping, appeal, and risk are supplied; proposing a reversible trial does not authorize implementation.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

2.10Methodological Boundaries for Multi-Circle Objects ​

In briefDrawing more circles does not automatically improve an explanation. Yet a circle’s failure to help prediction does not mean that its membership facts, responsibilities, or authority do not exist. State the purpose first.
Codes used in this section (1)
  • G1Conditional Gain from Candidate Grouping

Circles[5] are first of all candidate groupings, not natural entities established by naming. Families, organizations, platform groups, occupational communities, or cultural categories should specify boundaries, members, roles, channels, time windows, and identity criteria. Documents, relationship records, or exposure records can support the relevant facts about objects. A claim that the grouping brings explanatory or foresight gains must then be compared against suitable simple baselines, such as no grouping or a single circle. Formal G1 support does not replace other grounds for the object's existence. Parallelism, nesting, and overlap are judged along the declared dimensions. Potential bridging, actual transmission, and effects of transmission require separate evidence. Competition specifies constraints on the available set; temporariness specifies a time limit or evidence concerning duration. Both can be combined with other relations.

Multi-circle analysis must not turn every background factor into an entity. Before a circle is added, the necessary question it answers, the distinction that would be lost if it were removed, and the measurement and privacy costs should be stated. If it is used for explanation or propagation, the relevant channels and competing explanations must also be specified. Where its current purpose cannot be stated, retain it as an environmental condition or candidate variable. When a complex model lacks stable comparative support, reduce the relevant gain claims and give priority to an adequate simple model. Retaining an object to describe supported responsibilities, differences in membership, or authority over matters does not first require proving that it increases predictive accuracy.

2.10Note

Understanding this section

2.10 Methodological Boundaries for Objects with Multiple Circles

Drawing more circles does not automatically improve an explanation. Yet a circle’s failure to help prediction does not mean that its membership facts, responsibilities, or authority do not exist. State the purpose first.

Families, organizations, platform groups, professional communities, and cultural categories must first be declared as explicit objects: boundaries, members, roles, channels, time window, and K identity criterion. A name or clustering result does not itself create a natural entity; documents, relationships, and exposure records can nevertheless each support the relevant object facts, which cannot all be denied because G1 support is not yet available.

A claim that a grouping adds explanatory or anticipatory value requires comparison against appropriately simple baselines, such as no grouping or a single circle; formal G1 qualification must be established separately under its contract. The question here is ‘Does this grouping help with this task?’, which differs from ‘Does this family or institution have documents and membership relationships?’ One may be supported while the other remains unsupported.

Parallel, nested, and overlapping relations require a declared dimension of comparison. Overlapping member sets do not imply overlapping authority; spatial containment does not imply organizational subordination; two circles parallel in one dimension may share members in another. Competition describes constraints on feasible sets, meaning restrictions on available actions or resource conditions within a window; temporary describes duration or persistence. Both can coexist with nesting, overlap, and other relations, rather than being mutually exclusive labels.

Potential bridging, actual transmission, and transmission effects each require separate evidence. A person belonging to two groups may constitute a potential bridge; claiming that a message, resource, or exposure actually crossed requires an actual event; claiming that this transmission caused an outcome additionally requires causal comparison and mechanism material. An edge or a shared member does not prove propagation, much less establish that the transmitter necessarily bears all responsibility.

Before adding a circle, explain which necessary question it answers, what distinction would be lost if it were removed, and the added measurement and privacy costs. If it merely circles every background factor without an identifiable use, retain it provisionally as an environmental condition or variable candidate. When a complex model lacks stable comparative support, reduce the corresponding gain claim and prefer a sufficiently adequate simple model.

A circle may also be retained for supported responsibilities, member differences, or authority over particular matters; predictive accuracy is not an entry requirement for these uses. Simplifying a predictive model should not incidentally remove people’s rights or real organizational boundaries. Description, prediction, and normative governance must each meet their own evidentiary and authorization requirements.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Premise: a grouping may have membership or documentary support, or may merely be proposed by the analyst; these two object statuses must remain distinct.

  2. 2

    Separate uses: obtain the relevant records when describing members and authority; make proportionate baseline comparisons when claiming grouping gain; check channels, events, and effects when claiming a propagation mechanism.

  3. 3

    Check relations: determine parallel, nested, and overlapping relations along declared dimensions such as membership, space, organization, or authority; record competitive constraints and duration separately.

  4. 4

    Assess complexity: an added circle must preserve a necessary distinction at proportionate cost; absent stable gain evidence, do not exaggerate predictive value, while retaining independently supported membership, rights, and responsibility facts.

  5. 5

    Conclusion: multiple circles organize objects relative to a task. More names do not make objects more real, and predictive scores do not determine whether every object merits retention.

Distinctions to keep clear

Object facts

What membership, relationships, documents, or exposure records support.

≠

Grouping gain

What a grouping explains or predicts beyond the baseline, requiring a separate comparison.

Shared member / potential bridge

A particular possibility of connection exists.

≠

Actual transmission and its effect

Whether a specific event occurred and whether it affected the outcome require separate evidence.

Membership overlap

The sets have shared elements.

≠

Overlapping authority

Authorization for particular matters and actions intersects; this cannot be inferred from member sets.

A sufficiently adequate simple model

Less complexity for the current task.

≠

Removing objects of rights and responsibilities

A separate normative action that does not automatically follow from a lack of predictive gain.

Teaching set construction: overlap is not a single relationTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe people, circles, and actions are all teaching symbols; the action sets are supplied by assumption and do not constitute real authorization.

Let member circles A={甲,乙} and B={乙,丙}, so A∩B={乙}: the circles overlap in membership. If their permitted action sets for a matter are U_A={a,b} and U_B={b,c}, the action satisfying both is b. If instead U_B={c}, the jointly feasible action set is empty. Whether membership overlap exists and whether action constraints are compatible are two different judgments; one cannot infer that 乙 is authorized to perform every action from membership in both circles.

BoundaryThis illustrates only set relations and constraints; it establishes no real organizations, rights, responsibilities, or actual transmission.

The Hampstead drinking-water record: spatial circles and exposure circles do not coincideDocumented case

Page 44 of Snow’s original work records a woman living in Hampstead who had not visited Broad Street for a long time but still received water from its pump by a daily cart (the original term is ‘cart’). The focus here is not to re-estimate the cause of disease, but to show that residential boundaries cannot directly substitute for actual water-supply exposure boundaries.

SourceSnow, second edition, 1855, Hampstead passagePrinted p. 44, Hampstead West End case paragraph, followed by the account of her niece’s drinking water and illnessReading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThis is Snow’s historical account based on family reports and registration records; this guide does not construct a population-wide network or treat the water-delivery edge alone as a net causal effect.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Empirical counterevidenceSnow records someone living in Hampstead who had not visited Broad Street for a long time but received pump water by a daily water cart (the original term is ‘cart’).

What it limitsGrouping solely by residence near the pump may miss actual exposure channels; geographic circles and water-supply exposure must be checked separately.

John Snow, 1855, Hampstead West End drinking-water account

Teaching counterexampleTeaching boundary case: a legally valid responsible party fails to improve a model’s predictive accuracy and is consequently removed from the responsibility register.

What it limitsThis treats predictive usefulness as the entry requirement for objects of rights and responsibilities; independently supported responsibility and authority over particular matters should be retained.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • A lack of G1 gain evidence does not revoke an object’s existence supported by documents or relationships; conversely, an institution’s real name does not prove its usefulness for a particular prediction.
  • The historical water-exposure case shows only that residential location and exposure channels may not coincide; it does not establish that every family or cross-circle relationship can transmit something.
  • When privacy costs make an additional circle unjustified, retain necessary unknowns and scope limitations rather than covertly collecting personal relationships to fill a table.

Scope and open questions

A concrete historical water-supply connection demonstrates the difference between spatial grouping and actual channels, making it suitable for questions about boundaries between multiple circles; it is not elevated into a universal network mechanism.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    If adding a circle does not improve prediction, can its membership records be rejected on that basis?

  2. 2

    Does a person’s simultaneous membership in two groups suffice to prove that a message has spread?

  3. 3

    If two circles’ memberships overlap, can they directly be labeled as having ‘overlapping jurisdiction’?

If adding a circle does not improve prediction, can its membership records be rejected on that basis?

No. What is downgraded is the corresponding predictive-gain claim; real membership and documentary relationships retain their existing bases.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Does a person’s simultaneous membership in two groups suffice to prove that a message has spread?

No. Start with a potential bridge, then check the actual message, timing, and receipt; effects require further evidence.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If two circles’ memberships overlap, can they directly be labeled as having ‘overlapping jurisdiction’?

No. Authorization must be checked for specific objects, matters, actions, and durations; intersecting memberships cannot substitute for it.

2.11Methodological Boundaries for Personality and Actor States ​

In briefAn instance of silence, enthusiasm, or a score is initially material from a particular time and setting. Interpreting it as stable personality requires additional checks across time, contexts, measurements, and uses.

Personality enters only as a slow-variable hypothesis with an evidential level, not as an ontological definition of a person. A single behavior, self-report, report by someone else, scale score, or model-generated cluster cannot by itself establish a stable personality. Analysis must also retain competing explanations such as role activation, material constraints, immediate emotions, strategies, cultural norms, observer position, and measurement bias.

Actor variables are divided by timescale into slow, intermediate, and fast bands. Each is tied to an observation window, source, counterevidence, circle conditions, privacy, and permitted uses. The framework does not perform clinical or psychiatric diagnosis, nor does it record silence, refusal to disclose, or unobservability as pathological evidence. A model may propose candidate variables and minimal tests; it must not automatically fill in real-world values.

2.11Note

Understanding this section

2.11 Methodological Boundaries for Personality and Actor States

An instance of silence, enthusiasm, or a score is initially material from a particular time and setting. Interpreting it as stable personality requires additional checks across time, contexts, measurements, and uses.

This section places personality in the position of ‘a slow-variable hypothesis with an evidence level’, rather than fixing a person as an essence. Behavior may include relatively persistent tendencies, but one action, self-report, report by others, scale score, or model cluster cannot by itself generate a conclusion about stable personality. Naming a category cannot replace evidence across windows, contexts, and measurements.

At minimum, retain competing explanations involving role activation, material constraints, immediate emotion, strategy, cultural norms, observer position, and measurement bias. Similar reticence can occur during a task requiring concentration, in an unfamiliar language, or in a discussion where someone does not wish to disclose information; a single manifestation does not distinguish these explanations. Listing candidates does not claim that any of them actually occurred.

The slow, medium, and fast time bands help prevent substitutions of time scale: the slow band concerns hypotheses of persistent tendencies requiring longer windows of support; the medium band may concern temporary roles, goals, or resource states; the fast band may concern current emotion and local interaction. These scales are declared for the task and object, rather than forming a universal day-count table for everyone or automatically averaging fast variables into slow personality traits.

Each variable must be bound to an observation window, sources, disconfirming evidence, circle conditions, privacy, and permitted uses. Across settings, ask whether the original behavioral opportunities and roles remain, whether reports are comparable, and whether the inference exceeds the consented use. Multiple sources merely retelling one event cannot masquerade as repeated observation across contexts.

The framework does not make clinical or psychiatric diagnoses; silence, refusal to disclose, and unobservability are not evidence of pathology. A model may propose variable candidates and minimal tests, but cannot assign values to real people, much less expand managerial authority through inference. A careful result may be: ‘The available material is insufficient to distinguish a persistent tendency from a contextual response.’

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Premise: observed behavior is material concerning a person, time, setting, and observation method; it does not directly equal a stable cross-context attribute.

  2. 2

    Connection: a stable-tendency hypothesis requires an appropriate time window and comparable repeated material, and must compete with explanations involving roles, constraints, emotion, strategy, and measurement.

  3. 3

    Evidence classification: separately record the scope supported by self-reports, reports from others, scales, behavioral records, and model outputs; do not count one source or event repeatedly as evidence.

  4. 4

    Conclusion: at most, retain slow-variable candidates within supported windows, contexts, and uses; explanations not yet distinguished remain unresolved and cannot be elevated into a person’s fixed essence.

  5. 5

    Responsibility for use: any further collection or use of information involving privacy and action requires separate checks of necessity and authority; this section’s knowledge framework confers no qualification to diagnose or take personnel action.

Distinctions to keep clear

Current state

Behavior or self-report within a particular window.

≠

Slow-variable hypothesis

A relatively persistent tendency across windows, requiring more, proportionate evidence.

A mean describing a distribution

One summary of repeated manifestations.

≠

Always like this

A strong prediction about individual actions that does not follow from an average.

Scale or cluster label

A measurement or model representation.

≠

A person’s essence and clinical diagnosis

Neither can be generated by a label, and clinical diagnosis also lies outside this framework’s remit.

Unwillingness to disclose

A person’s boundary on information use.

≠

Evidence of pathology or a trait

Requires independent, qualified grounds and cannot be inferred from refusal itself.

Teaching mathematical construction: the same mean does not mean every occasion is identicalTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe numbers are constructed scores in the same units; A and B are not actual participants, and no clinical meaning is assigned.

Assume, solely to illustrate aggregation, that person A’s four state scores are 1,1,7,7 and person B’s are 4,4,4,4. Both means are 4, but their variability differs. Knowing the mean alone does not reveal a particular occasion’s score; moreover, four observations with unspecified contexts cannot establish any real personality from this setup.

BoundaryThe example only refutes ‘same mean → same behavioral distribution / identical behavior every time’; it provides no evidence about real personality.

Teaching candidate: one refusal to speakTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe situation is entirely hypothetical; the candidates are not judgments about any actual person.

For the hypothetical scene “someone declines to speak at a meeting,” candidate explanations include: their role does not require speaking, insufficient material, current fatigue, strategic withholding, unwillingness to disclose here, or a more persistent preference. That behavior alone cannot select among these, still less establish a conclusion about health or personality. First ask whether the current task actually requires more personal information.

BoundaryNo compelled disclosure or unauthorized testing is recommended. Remaining unknown is a legitimate result.

A 2001 experience-sampling study: state variation and aggregate stability coexistDocumented case

In three experience-sampling studies with students, Fleeson repeatedly collected self-reports of everyday behavior over approximately two to three weeks. The research found both within-person variation and stability of aggregate distribution parameters. ‘Stability’ here mainly comes from random split-half comparisons within the same observation window, not proof of lifelong invariance.

SourceWilliam Fleeson, 2001, Traits as Density Distributions of StatesJPSP 80(6):1011–1027; abstract on p. 1011; methods on pp. 1014–1015, 1019–1020, 1022; Table 4 note on p. 1020 and discussion on pp. 1023–1024Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThe original work is a short-window self-report study and offers no personality diagnosis of this guide’s readers or any specified person. Split-half stability has not been described as lifelong stability, and the raw data were not recalculated.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Empirical counterevidenceFleeson's three experience-sampling studies in 2001 report both substantial within-person state variation and stability in aggregated distribution parameters.

What it limitsShort-term variation and aggregate stability can coexist. Neither a single behavior nor one average covers every situation.

Fleeson, Toward a Structure- and Process-Integrated View of Personality: Traits as Density Distributions of States

Teaching counterexampleTeaching boundary: an observer records refusal to provide private information as “evidence of avoidant personality.”

What it limitsRefusal to disclose is not standalone evidence of pathology or stable personality. Withdraw the label and retain the information boundary.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Fleeson’s experience-sampling research uses students’ self-reports; stability of aggregate parameters is assessed mainly through random split-half comparisons within the same short window. It cannot be said to prove lifelong personality invariance or predictability of every action.
  • Insufficient material does not mean that the person has no persistent tendencies; it only limits the judgments currently available.
  • The examples in this section must not be used to score a particular real person’s personality, assert their mental state, or conduct high-impact screening; this guide has measured no reader.

Scope and open questions

A primary experience-sampling design can illustrate the different temporal meanings of states and aggregated tendencies. It is suitable as an example of methodological boundaries, not a personality test.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Is one enthusiastic instance sufficient to establish that someone is stably extraverted?

  2. 2

    Does a highly stable mean of repeated reports mean that every moment is the same?

  3. 3

    If a person is unwilling to disclose information, may a model automatically fill in health or personality information from other weak clues?

Is one enthusiastic instance sufficient to establish that someone is stably extraverted?

No. One performance covers only its immediate situation. Comparable material across multiple windows and competing explanations are needed, and the use must be justified.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Does a highly stable mean of repeated reports mean that every moment is the same?

No. A stable mean can coexist with substantial within-person variation. Distribution and context also matter.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If a person is unwilling to disclose information, may a model automatically fill in health or personality information from other weak clues?

No. Retain the unknown and examine necessity, privacy, and use. Silence cannot be treated as evidence of pathology or as authorization to infer.

2.12Methodological Boundaries for Foresight and Projection ​

In briefProjections may be richly developed, but the factual record cannot change along with imagination. Evaluating foresight requires knowing what was actually known at the time, what prediction was committed to, and when it counts as right or wrong.

Path projection may use observations, reports, plans, hypothetical events, and simulated events, but must retain the event type. A report's content is not automatically true; a plan is not the same as execution; hypothetical and simulated events are not written back as real-world facts. Each run freezes the joint snapshot, evidence cutoff, mechanisms, parameter ranges, clocks, propagation rules, and stopping conditions. Information obtained after the results may enter only a new version.

Conditional foresight must register, before results, the target, horizon, scope of objects and circles, input cutoff, simple baseline, paths, form of expression, calibration metrics, early signals, contrary signals, suspension, retirement, and outcome write-back. Unregistered post hoc explanations do not count as successful predictions. Changing the target, extending the horizon, narrowing the population, or merging paths all require a new record. For reopening on stated grounds, see §2.14.

2.12Note

Understanding this section

2.12 Methodological boundaries for foresight and projection

Projections may be richly developed, but the factual record cannot change along with imagination. Evaluating foresight requires knowing what was actually known at the time, what prediction was committed to, and when it counts as right or wrong.

Projection inputs may include observations, reports, plans, assumptions, and simulated events, but must retain their types. Observations have measurement limitations; a report establishes that someone said something, while its content still requires verification. A plan concerns intended action and cannot be recorded as execution. Assumptions and simulations enter the model only under their corresponding conditions and must not rewrite what actually happened. Entry into the same execution interface does not make materials equally true or evidentially equivalent.

Each run freezes a joint snapshot: object and circle states, evidence cutoff, mechanisms, parameter ranges, clocks, propagation rules, and stopping conditions. Distinguish particularly when an event occurred from when the researcher learned of it. Material learned afterward cannot quietly be inserted into the inputs available to an earlier foresight run, even when it describes an earlier event.

Before outcomes occur, conditional foresight registers its target, horizon, object and circle scope, input cutoff, simple baseline, paths, expression format, calibration metrics, early signals, contrary signals, suspension, retirement, and outcome write-back. “Things will improve later” is insufficiently evaluable: specify which quantity improves, within what period, for whom, and relative to what.

Multiple paths are not an insurance box from which to choose a hit afterward. Their expression and aggregation must be specified beforehand. One cannot change the target, extend the horizon, narrow the population, or merge paths after the outcome and count the new answer as the old version's success. New information can improve the next version; the old version remains evaluated under its original contract with its deviations retained.

Calibration differs from a single hit. Failure of one high-probability event to occur does not immediately establish overall miscalibration; one hit does not establish long-term model superiority either. Accumulate tests using preselected scoring, baselines, and evaluation units, accounting for dependence among events. A change in conditions or evaluation units may change the target being evaluated.

This section does not prohibit simulation or planning. Simulation explores consequences of assumptions; plans indicate possible future events; updates reflect new knowledge. The key is preserving status and versions. The real example below shows only why counterfactual simulation figures in a paper cannot be described as actual implementation outcomes. It does not claim that the paper constitutes a future prediction passing this framework's contract.

Freezing the evaluation target still allows reasoned challenges to the question itself. Under §2.14, if new evidence exposes affected people omitted by the original representation or mistaken constraints, a separate question may be established. Preserve the old input cutoff, target, and performance record, and state whether the new and old questions replace, parallel, or refine one another. An unfavorable result alone does not justify turning an old prediction into a success.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Premise: prediction evaluation requires a locatable commitment made before the outcome and the information set available then. Otherwise prediction cannot be distinguished from retrospective explanation.

  2. 2

    Freezing: specify the input cutoff, object snapshot, mechanisms and parameters, event clocks, and stopping rules; preserve material types.

  3. 3

    Public projection: generate conditional paths or probabilities from declared inputs and rules without labeling intermediate simulated nodes as real observations.

  4. 4

    Evaluation: compare actual outcomes and the preset baseline under the original horizon and target. New information enters only a new version and does not rewrite old inputs or success conditions.

  5. 5

    Conclusion: conditional foresight and simulated consequences may be offered, but used only according to their status. Actual action additionally requires independent evidence, norms, and authorization.

Distinctions to keep clear

Report

A source claims something occurred; its truth requires verification.

≠

Observed fact

Has corresponding observational grounds while retaining measurement boundaries.

Plan

An arrangement intended for implementation.

≠

Execution

The action and timing that actually occurred, requiring event records.

Simulation result

Consequences calculated under a model and parameters.

≠

Actual effectiveness

Material and causal grounds concerning real execution and outcomes.

New foresight version

A separate run under new information or conditions.

≠

Rewriting an old hit

Treating retrospective changes as earlier success undermines evaluation.

Teaching construction: late-arriving information can produce only a new versionTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe project, dates, stoppage, and outcome are all teaching assumptions and refer to no actual construction project.

Suppose V1 closes its information set on June 1 and predicts that the same project will satisfy specified acceptance conditions by September 30. A report saying “work already stopped in August” arrives only on October 5. It concerns an earlier event but was not known input to V1. After verification, it may enter V2 or explain V1's deviation; one cannot claim V1 already used it. If construction finishes in November, V1's horizon still cannot be changed to year-end to report a hit.

BoundaryIllustrates only versioning and the distinction between two kinds of time; it evaluates no real project.

Mathematical teaching construction: specify the scoring rule first rather than selecting a preferred oneTeaching scenario

AssumptionsProbabilities, outcome, and scoring are all teaching stipulations. No actual foresight exercise was conducted.

Suppose it is agreed beforehand to score a binary outcome y by squared error (p−y)², with lower scores better. For one forecast p=0.8 and outcome y=0, the score is 0.64; a baseline p=0.5 scores 0.25 on the same event. This shows only that the former performs worse on that occasion under the preset rule. It does not establish that it is worse across every task or globally miscalibrated.

BoundaryA single score cannot stand for overall calibration, nor may a favorable scoring rule be substituted after the outcome.

17.7% and 46.5% in the 2019 algorithm paper: counterfactual rearrangementDocumented case

At the 97th-percentile threshold, Obermeyer and colleagues used counterfactual rearrangement to estimate that the proportion of Black patients among those automatically identified would change from 17.7% to 46.5%. The original explicitly describes a simulated scenario, not an observed improvement following actual implementation.

SourceObermeyer et al. 2019, counterfactual simulation and Fig.1BScience 366:447–453; printed p.449, counterfactual simulation paragraph preceding Fig.1B and its caption; PDF page 3Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThe denominator is those automatically identified at the specified threshold, not all patients. The result concerns simulated selection composition, not actual additional care, individual health, or long-term effects. This lesson did not recalculate the data.

Read the case and sources

What counterexamples change

Empirical counterevidenceIn Obermeyer and colleagues' 2019 paper, the change from 17.7% to 46.5% is the estimated proportion of Black patients among automatically identified patients under counterfactual rearrangement at the 97th-percentile threshold.

What it limitsThis is a simulated composition change, not an observed improvement in care following actual implementation.

Obermeyer et al. 2019, counterfactual simulation passage

Teaching counterexampleTeaching boundary: an original prediction concerns improvement for an entire population by year-end; after the outcome, only improving subgroups are selected and the horizon is extended by six months, yet the original prediction is counted as a hit.

What it limitsThe target population and horizon have changed. A new record is required; evaluate the original prediction under its original contract.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • A counterfactual calculation rearranging patient composition does not establish actual algorithm modification, increased actual care, or improved health. The source's status must be retained.
  • A probability forecast's single success or failure does not establish overall calibration. Sample dependence, mixing tasks, and selective reporting also affect evaluation.
  • A frozen snapshot guarantees neither correct mechanisms nor execution without deviation. It supplies fixed, reviewable grounds; execution and counterexamples still require subsequent examination.

Scope and open questions

The actual paper explicitly distinguishes original grouping from simulated rearrangement, making it suitable for testing “simulation does not write back into reality.” It is not presented as a foresight experiment completed by this lesson.

  • Claiming that real deployment changed care and health requires subsequent implementation, time-window and outcome material, and corresponding comparisons of effects. This lesson does not possess those materials.

A report says an event happened yesterday but arrives today. May yesterday's prediction treat it as a known input?

No. Event time differs from information-arrival time. After verification, the report enters a new version; the old version retains its original information cutoff.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If a paper's simulation shows that a proportion would increase, may one write “the proportion increased after implementation”?

No. Simulation is neither execution nor observation; actual implementation and outcome material are required.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If the original deadline was September 30 and the target was reached only in October, may the horizon be changed to count the original prediction as correct?

No. A new horizon creates a new record. Close the original version under its original horizon; causes may be explained, but a hit may not be rewritten.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above
